about.title: About Liam Perry and the Personal Injury Law Uncovered Podcast
about.description: Liam Perry founded Perry Personal Injury Lawyers after years working as an insurance defense litigator for several of the largest carriers in the country. The firm represents injured Californians from seven offices across Southern California, with headquarters in downtown San Diego. The Personal Injury Law Uncovered podcast extends that work — every episode walks San Diego drivers through what the adjuster is actually thinking, how demand packages are evaluated, and what California law (SR-1, pure comparative negligence, the two-year statute) means for their claim.

attorney.name: Liam Perry
attorney.title: Founding Attorney & Podcast Host
bio: Liam Perry is the founding attorney of Perry Personal Injury Lawyers and host of Personal Injury Law Uncovered. Before building the firm, Liam spent years as an insurance defense litigator for several of the largest carriers in the country. He now brings that insider's view to the other side of the table, representing injured Californians from seven offices across Southern California with his headquarters in downtown San Diego.

Liam's practice focuses on serious car, truck, motorcycle, rideshare, bicycle, and pedestrian accident cases, plus wrongful death and catastrophic injury matters. He has recovered more than $30 million for injured clients and is routinely co-counseled by other firms on complex cases. His approach pairs former-defense-counsel rigor with plain-language client communication, so injured Californians understand what the adjuster is doing at every step of their claim.

Beyond his practice, Liam hosts Personal Injury Law Uncovered to give San Diego drivers the insider's view no general-market podcast can offer. Each episode anchors to California law and San Diego roadways, covers the decisions listeners face in the first 72 hours after a crash, and translates every piece of jargon the first time it appears (comparative negligence, demand package, UM/UIM, pre-litigation) so the audience leaves more prepared than they were 50 minutes earlier.

content.articleTitle: The Insider's View of San Diego Car Accident Claims
articleParagraphs: Personal Injury Law Uncovered fills the gap every San Diego driver runs into when they start Googling after a crash. National-scope podcasts never speak to California law — no SR-1, no pure comparative negligence, no two-year statute. Local content is mostly thinly disguised law firm advertising that never teaches anyone anything. And most lawyer-hosted shows are produced by attorneys who have only ever worked the plaintiff side, without the insider's view of how adjusters actually evaluate claims. Liam Perry spent years as an insurance defense litigator for several of the largest carriers in the country before switching sides, which means every episode gets to use that insider lens.

Each episode anchors to a real scenario a San Diego driver is navigating right now (rear-ended on the 805, hit by an Uber near Petco Park, a dog bite on a walk through Balboa Park, a rideshare crash in Mission Valley) and walks through the decisions listeners have to make in the first 72 hours after the crash, then the first 30 days, then pre-litigation. Liam translates every term the first time it appears (comparative negligence, demand package, UM/UIM, pre-litigation) and anchors every statute to the California code section it actually comes from, so the audience can independently verify what they hear.
content.featuredQuote: I spent years deciding what insurance companies were going to pay on claims. Now I get to make sure San Diego drivers don't leave that money on the table.

episode.title: What Every San Diego Driver Needs to Know in the First 72 Hours After a Crash

questions.question: What Topics Does Liam Perry Cover on Personal Injury Law Uncovered?
questions.answer: Liam Perry covers everything a San Diego driver needs to know about California car accident claims, with rotation into truck, motorcycle, rideshare, bicycle, and pedestrian cases. Every episode anchors to California law (SR-1, pure comparative negligence, the two-year statute, UM/UIM) and to San Diego roadways from I-5 and the 805 through North County. Liam uses his former insurance-defense background to explain what the adjuster is actually thinking on each call.

questions.question: How Often Are New Episodes Released?
questions.answer: Personal Injury Law Uncovered publishes on a weekly, evergreen cadence. Episodes run 50 to 55 minutes each and are organized by practice area cluster — Car Accidents as the primary cluster, with Truck, Motorcycle, Rideshare, Bicycle, Pedestrian, and broader personal injury in rotation — rather than numbered seasons.

questions.question: Who is The Target Audience?
questions.answer: The show is built for San Diego drivers between 25 and 55 who have been in a car accident in the last 30 days or have a close family member who has. Secondary audiences include family members helping an injured loved one, referral sources like chiropractors and physical therapists who want a lawyer they can confidently send patients to, and other San Diego attorneys screening potential co-counsel on catastrophic cases.

questions.question: Can I Submit Questions for The Podcast?
questions.answer: Yes. Liam welcomes listener questions and case scenarios through perrypi.com. The show regularly addresses common questions from San Diego accident victims, and many episodes are shaped directly by what listeners are asking. The podcast provides general legal information and cannot replace individualized legal advice about your specific matter.

faqGroups.label: California Car Accident Questions
faqGroups.description: Common legal questions about car accident claims in San Diego and throughout California.

questions.question: How Long Do I Have to File a Car Accident Claim in California?
questions.answer: California's statute of limitations for most personal injury claims, including car accidents, is two years from the date of the injury. Property-damage-only claims generally run three years. Claims against California government entities require a written claim within six months and are governed by the Government Claims Act. Liam recommends contacting an attorney promptly to preserve evidence and meet every deadline that applies to your specific matter.

questions.question: What is SR-1 and Do I Need to File One After a California Accident?
questions.answer: SR-1 is the Report of Traffic Accident Occurring in California, filed with the California DMV. You are required to file it within 10 days if anyone was injured or killed, or if property damage to any person's property exceeded $1,000 — independent of whether the police came to the scene. Failing to file can result in a license suspension, so it is one of the first things Liam walks clients through after a crash.

questions.question: What if I Was Partly at Fault For The Accident?
questions.answer: California follows pure comparative negligence, which means you can still recover even if you were the majority at fault for the crash — your recovery just gets reduced by your share of responsibility. Adjusters will try to assign you a higher percentage of fault than the facts support, because every point they add subtracts from what they pay. Liam's former defense experience is specifically useful for pushing back on those fault allocations.

questions.question: The Other Driver Was Uninsured or Underinsured. Am I Out of Options?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. California insurers are required to offer Uninsured and Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM) coverage, so if you carry it — or if another household policy does — that coverage can step into the gap. Liam walks through UM/UIM in multiple episodes because it is one of the most misunderstood parts of a California claim.
